title: Separating function fields and the geometrically integral generic curve
statement:
Let $k\subseteq F\subseteq L\subseteq E$ be fields, with $E/k$ and $F/k$ finitely generated, $E/F$ separably generated of transcendence degree one, and $L/F$ finite. Assume $L$ is algebraically closed in $E$: every element of $E$ algebraic over $L$ lies in $L$. Let $g:T\to Y$ be a proper dominant $k$-morphism of integral finite-type $k$-schemes, with $T$ normal, together with identifications $k(T)=E$ and $k(Y)=L$ under which the map on function fields is the displayed inclusion. Then $L/F$ is finite separable, $E/L$ is separably generated of transcendence degree one, and the generic fibre $C=T\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}L$ is a proper normal geometrically integral finite-type $L$-scheme with function field $E$ and dimension one. Moreover $\dim Y=\operatorname{trdeg}_k F$ and $\dim T=\operatorname{trdeg}_k F+1$. No smoothness of $C/L$ is asserted. Here separably generated means admitting a finite transcendence basis over which the remaining algebraic extension is finite separable.

The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-kun-transcendence-degree], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. A projective morphism here means an H-projective morphism: it admits a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over its target. A semilinear $H$-action means actions by scheme automorphisms and by field automorphisms of $k$, with the structure morphisms equivariant; faithfulness is not assumed. A birational morphism here identifies the function fields and is an isomorphism over a dense open of the target.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-separable] to $E/F$. Since $L/F$ is finite, it is a finitely generated subextension, so the conclusion says that $L/F$ admits a separating transcendence basis. A finite extension is algebraic: the powers of each element are linearly dependent in the finite-dimensional $F$-vector space $L$. Thus its transcendence degree is zero by [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower], and its transcendence basis is empty. Its remaining algebraic extension is therefore $L/F$ itself, which is separable. This proves the first assertion.

By the hypothesis and [def-kun-transcendence-degree], a separating transcendence basis for $E/F$ has one element $t$. Thus $E/F(t)$ is finite separable. The element $t$ remains transcendental over $L$: otherwise $L(t)/L$ and $L/F$ would both be finite-dimensional, making $t$ algebraic over $F$. An $F(t)$-spanning family for $E$ also spans it over $L(t)$, so $E/L(t)$ is finite. For $a\in E$, let $P$ and $Q$ be its minimal polynomials over $F(t)$ and $L(t)$. Division by the monic $Q$ gives $P=QR$ in $L(t)[X]$: the remainder vanishes at $a$ and has smaller degree than $Q$, hence is zero by minimality. Choose $U,V\in F(t)[X]$ with $UP+VP^{\prime}=1$. Since $P^{\prime}=Q^{\prime}R+QR^{\prime}$, we obtain $1=Q(UR+VR^{\prime})+Q^{\prime}(VR)$ in $L(t)[X]$. Thus $Q$ is separable. Therefore $t$ is a separating basis for $E/L$, its transcendence degree is one, and $E/L$ is finitely generated (a basis of the finite $L(t)$-vector space $E$, together with $t$, generates it as a field).

proof.text: Let $\eta_Y$ and $\eta_T$ be the generic points, and $j:C\to T$ the projection. The function-field-map convention gives $g(\eta_T)=\eta_Y$, with generic stalk map the prescribed $L\subseteq E$. The generic fibre $C$ is irreducible by [lem-zl-irreducible-dominant-generic-fibre]. It is proper over $L$ by proper base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change], and consequently finite type over $L$ by the definition of properness.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, lemma-bertini-irreducible, generic-fibre argument; morphisms.tex Tag 01W4, lemma-base-change-proper

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-spectrum-base-change-stalks] to $g$ and $p=\eta_Y$, where $\mathcal O_{Y,p}=L$. Every point of $C$ maps to $p$, since $\operatorname{Spec}L$ has one point, so its local ring is canonically the local ring of $T$ at its image. All these rings are integrally closed domains. Thus $C$ is normal and reduced, and together with irreducibility from Step 3 it is integral. To identify its generic point, take any nonempty affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ and a nonempty affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}D\subseteq g^{-1}V$. These charts cover $C$. The same cited statement identifies $j^{-1}W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}D)$ for $S$ the image of $A\setminus\{0\}$. The affine fraction-field lemma and the given inclusion $L\subseteq E$ show $0\notin S$. The localization-domain lemma makes this chart integral, with zero prime lying over the zero prime of $D$. The unique lift of $\eta_T$ is therefore generic in each such chart, hence in $C$. The cited local-ring isomorphism at this lift gives $L$-algebraically $k(C)=\mathcal O_{C,\eta_C}\cong\mathcal O_{T,\eta_T}=E$, with the specified inclusion of $L$.

proof.text: For every field extension $K/L$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced] with $k=L$, the separably generated extension $E/L$ of Step 2, and the reduced $L$-algebra $S=K$. It gives that $E\otimes_LK$ is reduced. Step 4 identifies $E$ with the stalk at the unique generic point of the reduced scheme $C$. Hence [lem-pur-geometric-reducedness-from-generic-stalks] applies and proves that $C$ is geometrically reduced over $L$.

The subfield of $E$ consisting of elements separably algebraic over $L$ equals $L$, because such elements are algebraic over $L$ and $L$ is algebraically closed in $E$ by hypothesis. Since Step 2 makes $E/L$ finitely generated, [lem-zl-finite-separable-closure] therefore says that $\operatorname{Spec}E$ is geometrically irreducible over $L$. The generic stalk of $C$ is the field $E$ by Step 4; its maximal ideal is zero, so its residue field is $E$ with the same $L$-structure. Hence [lem-zl-generic-point-geometric-irreducibility] gives geometric irreducibility of $C$. For each extension $K/L$, $C_K$ is now both reduced and irreducible and is nonempty by irreducibility. The definitions give integrality of $C_K$, hence geometric integrality of $C$.

Apply [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] to each entire underlying closed subset of the finite-type integral schemes $C/L$, $Y/k$, and $T/k$. Their generic residue fields are their function fields $E$, $L$, and $E$. Thus $\dim C=\operatorname{trdeg}_LE=1$, $\dim Y=\operatorname{trdeg}_kL$, and $\dim T=\operatorname{trdeg}_kE$. Finiteness of $L/F$ gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_FL=0$; the tower formula gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_kL=\operatorname{trdeg}_kF$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_kE=\operatorname{trdeg}_kF+\operatorname{trdeg}_FE=\operatorname{trdeg}_kF+1$. These are the remaining assertions.

I read the item and all 24 distinct cited node statements. I checked them against Stacks 037Q (algebra.tex:11428), 054Q (varieties.tex:1446), 030U (algebra.tex:10152) and 030X. The delivery adds no new nodes, the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, there is no SGA citation, and parent lem-sfb-equivariant-curve-pencil step 5 uses exactly these clauses. Previous head 3b51eaed9 was returned only by the landing tool ('completed in this project's DAG but not in the live DAG'), not for any mathematical fault. This head differs from it only by fuller wording in Step 2 (Bezout identity) and Step 6 (residue field at the generic point); the uses lists are identical. Step 1: a finite L/F has trdeg 0, so its basis is empty, so L/F is separable. Step 2 is genuinely elementary: t stays transcendental over L, E/L(t) is finite, P=QR, and Q(UR+VR')+Q'(VR)=UP+VP'=1, so E/L is separably generated of trdeg 1 and finitely generated. Step 3: dominance gives g(eta_T)=eta_Y; 0G4F gives an irreducible fibre; proper base change works for any base map, so C is proper and of finite type. Step 4: every x in C lies over the closed point of Spec L, so it is the unique lift of h(x) and has the same local ring, hence normal, reduced and integral. In the chart, A to D embeds into L to E, so 0 is not in S and the zero prime of S^{-1}D is the generic point of C. The L-structures agree because c∘π=g∘h. Step 5: 030U applies to E/L with S a field, which feeds the generic-stalk criterion. Step 6: the separable closure of L in E is L, so 037Q and 054Q apply, giving geometric integrality. Step 7: 0B1C plus the tower formula gives dim C=1, dim Y=trdeg_k F and dim T=trdeg_k F+1. Edge cases: F=L=k with E=k(t); an inseparable L/F, which the hypotheses exclude; a larger constant field, which Step 6's hypothesis excludes; imperfect L, where smoothness is correctly not claimed. I accept the 8 off-unit tool_uses as general tools the route needs. Maintainer note: if L promotes the item, it should land this head.
